request.prompt: View 5, the same castle seen from high in the air to the south-west, looking north-east and down at about thirty degrees, at dusk in rain. In the right foreground the long stone bridge on piers comes in from the south and meets the gatehouse at the crag's south cliff. The key subject: a narrow stone shelf path, lit by a few lanterns, begins at a small door in the gatehouse's south face just to the left of where the bridge meets it, runs left (west) along the foot of the south curtain wall on a ledge cut into the sheer south cliff, turns the crag's south-west corner, and runs up the west cliff face, again on a ledge below the west curtain wall, to a small back door in the west end wall of a long slate-roofed stable block. Behind the walls: the big open courtyard, the cloister and tall chapel with its rose window on the left, the tall keep in the centre, and the slender bell tower at the far left back. Sixteen blocks of sheer cliff drop from the shelf to the misty valley floor.
